subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Successive percentage change, percentage error, population growth, salt mixtures

questions.stem: If the price of an article is increased by 20% and then DECREASED by 20%, the net effect on the original price is:
questions.explanation: Successive % shortcut: net change = a + b + ab/100. With a = +20, b = −20 → 20 − 20 + (−400/100) = 0 − 4 = −4%. Equivalently: 100 → 120 (after +20%) → 96 (after −20% of 120). Net change = (96−100)/100 = −4%. Distractor 1 is the common-sense WRONG answer (people assume they cancel). Distractor 3 has correct magnitude but wrong sign. Distractor 4 doubles correct value.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: If A's salary is 25% more than B's salary, by what percent is B's salary LESS than A's salary?
questions.explanation: Let B = 100 → A = 125. B is less than A by 25/125 × 100 = 20%. General formula: if A is x% more than B, then B is (100x/(100+x))% less than A. Here x = 25 → 2500/125 = 20%. Distractor 1 is the COMMON WRONG answer (% more and % less aren't symmetrical). Distractor 3 = 15% from another miscomputation. Distractor 4 = 30% from yet another error.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The population of a town is 10,000 and grows at 10% per year. After two years, the population will be:
questions.explanation: Compound growth: P(1 + r)ⁿ = 10000 × 1.1² = 10000 × 1.21 = 12,100. Year by year: Year 1 → 11,000 (10000 + 1000); Year 2 → 12,100 (11000 + 1100). Distractor 12,000 from simple-interest-style 10000 × (1 + 0.10×2) = 12,000 (uses simple interest formula). Distractor 11,000 stops at year 1. Distractor 12,200 from a different miscalculation.

questions.stem: 30% of a number is 60. What is 75% of the same number?
questions.explanation: 0.30 x = 60 → x = 200. 75% of 200 = 0.75 × 200 = 150. Distractor 100 = 50% (used wrong percentage). Distractor 200 = the original number (not the 75%). Distractor 175 from a calculation slip.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: In an exam a student got 35% marks and failed by 40 marks. Another student got 50% and passed with 35 marks more than the pass mark. The maximum marks of the exam are:
questions.explanation: Let max marks = M, pass mark = P. From student 1: 0.35M = P − 40 → P = 0.35M + 40. From student 2: 0.50M = P + 35 → P = 0.50M − 35. Equate: 0.35M + 40 = 0.50M − 35 → 75 = 0.15M → M = 500. Pass mark = 0.35(500)+40 = 215. Verify: 0.5(500) = 250 = 215+35 ✓. Distractor 400 from M = 75/0.1875 (rounded). Distractor 450 from miscomputed difference. Distractor 600 from M = 90/0.15.

questions.stem: A's income is 20% more than B's. If B's income is 25% less than C's, then A's income is what percent of C's?
questions.explanation: Let C = 100. B = 100 − 25 = 75 (25% less than C). A = 1.20 × 75 = 90 (20% more than B). So A is 90% of C. Distractor 85% from miscomputed 0.85 × 100. Distractor 100% incorrect intuition. Distractor 95% from different chain.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A solution contains 20% salt by weight. After evaporating some water, the salt concentration becomes 25%. The fraction of original water that was evaporated is:
questions.explanation: Take 100 g solution: 20 g salt + 80 g water. After evaporation salt is unchanged (20 g) but concentration is 25%, so total solution = 20/0.25 = 80 g. Water now = 80 − 20 = 60 g. Evaporated water = 80 − 60 = 20 g. Fraction of original water evaporated = 20/80 = 1/4. Distractor 1/5 from 20/100. Distractor 1/6 from another denominator slip. Distractor 1/3 from miscalculating final water as 40 g.
